svg.title: The evolution of the universe
svg.desc: A timeline of the universe on a compressed, roughly logarithmic scale, widening to the right like the expanding universe, with time across the top and the typical particle energy along the bottom. From the left: a hypothetical theory-of-everything era near 10^−43 s and 10^19 GeV with complete symmetry; a proposed grand-unified era; spontaneous symmetry breaking and inflation, 10^−35 to 10^−32 s; the electroweak era of leptons, quarks, W and Z bosons and photons down to 100 GeV at 10^−11 s; then leptons, hadrons and photons through the quark, lepton and photon eras and nucleosynthesis (10^−6 s to 100 s); light nuclei and atoms by about 3.8 × 10^5 y; stars and protogalaxies near 10^8 y; galaxies by 10^9 y; the Earth at about 9.2 × 10^9 y, life by about 10^10 y, and now, 1.38 × 10^10 y.
